objectives.text: Singers arrive at rehearsal with their own parts to hand
Volunteers are not tied up keeping the service running

rejected.label: Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app
rejected.note: Important because it puts the music where singers already look before rehearsal; a way of helping a singer find their part, judged through singer-part-finding. The user said it must sync, so it may also be a veto; asked in questions.

rejected.label: Dark mode
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because the brochures list it.

rejected.label: Works offline
rejected.note: Nobody raised it; only one brochure lists it. Asked in questions in case singers need parts without a connection.

anchors.text: A source states that a singer must search or browse the whole library by title to find a part.
A source states that a singer can filter the library to one voice or one piece, and must then pick their own part from the list.
A source states that a singer can open their own voice part directly from a per-voice view, with no search.

definition.objective: Singers arrive at rehearsal with their own parts to hand
definition.question: How many steps does a singer need to reach their own part from the app?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation or product pages describing how singers navigate to parts; a reviewer's general praise of the app does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a singer finds a part.
Sources disagree about how a singer reaches a part.

exclusions: Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app: judge the singer's search, not the calendar link.
How fast the app loads or how it looks; neither is about finding a part.

anchors.text: A source states that a volunteer must update the library by hand every week.
A source states that a volunteer must update the library by hand, such as at the start of each season.
A source states that the provider keeps the library up to date, and that volunteers only manage their own folders.

definition.objective: Volunteers are not tied up keeping the service running
definition.question: How often must a volunteer keep the library up to date by hand?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of who updates the library and how often; a statement that does not say who does the update does not count.

missingRules.when: No source says who keeps the library up to date.
Sources disagree about who must keep the library up to date.

exclusions: The price of the service, which is not about volunteer time.
Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app: the calendar link is judged in singer-part-finding, not here.

provenance.quote: Singers need to find their parts quickly before rehearsal.
We can't afford anything that needs a volunteer to maintain it every week.

questions: You said the service must sync with the rehearsal calendar app. It is treated here as a way of helping singers find their parts before rehearsal. Is it instead a hard requirement, so that a service without the sync is ruled out whatever else it does?

You said you can't afford anything that needs a volunteer to maintain it every week. Is that a hard limit that rules out a service needing weekly upkeep whatever else it does, or a preference to weigh against the others?
Only two criteria come from what you said. Is there anything else the choir needs the service to do?
Do singers need their parts without a phone or internet connection, for example at the rehearsal hall? Offline mode is in one brochure and nobody has said whether it matters.
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?

objectives.text: The team has its parts before its competition deadlines
Volunteer mentors' time goes to the team, not to chasing orders

rejected.label: Orders go through the school's purchase-order system
rejected.note: The user gave no reason for the requirement. The only objective it could serve here is mentor time, so it is judged through mentor-ordering-effort if it is a means at all; it may instead be a veto. Asked in questions.

rejected.label: Branding
rejected.note: The user said: 'Forget about branding, we don't care.'

rejected.label: Loyalty points
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because all three brochures list loyalty rewards. Asked in questions in case it matters.

anchors.text: A source states that orders take more than two weeks to arrive.
A source states that stocked items dispatch the next day, and that other items take one to two weeks.
A source states that every item dispatches within two days, with a stated delivery time.

definition.objective: The team has its parts before its competition deadlines
definition.question: How long does a part take to reach the team after it is ordered?
definition.evidenceRule: The supplier's stated dispatch or delivery times; a customer review's delivery anecdote does not count.

missingRules.when: No source states dispatch or delivery times.
Sources give conflicting dispatch or delivery times.

exclusions: How the order is placed or tracked; that is mentor-ordering-effort.

anchors.text: A source states that orders can only be placed or checked by phone or email.
A source states that orders can be placed and tracked online, but the buyer must confirm each order by hand.
A source states that a school account places orders online and sends status updates to the buyer without the buyer checking.

definition.objective: Volunteer mentors' time goes to the team, not to chasing orders
definition.question: How much of the buyer's time does placing and tracking an order take?
definition.evidenceRule: The supplier's documentation of how orders are placed, confirmed and tracked; a review's remark about the website alone does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how an order is placed or tracked.
Sources disagree on how an order is placed or tracked.

exclusions: Orders go through the school's purchase-order system: asked in questions, not judged here.

provenance.quote: We need parts to arrive before competition deadlines.
Mentors are volunteers and can't spend evenings chasing orders.

questions: Everything has to be ordered through the school's purchase-order system. Why? Is that a hard requirement, so that a supplier that cannot take purchase orders is ruled out whatever else it does?
Which deadlines matter, and how many days before each one must parts arrive? Delivery speed cannot be judged without a window.
You said forget about branding. Loyalty points are in all three brochures. Do points or rewards matter to the team or school, or should they be ignored too?
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion, or already settled by the school's budget? One supplier advertises bulk discounts.
Only two criteria come from what you said. Is there anything else the mentors or the team need from the supplier?

objectives.text: Members get a tool when they need it
The society's tools are not lost

rejected.label: Has a mobile app
rejected.note: The user gave no reason for the requirement. The only objective it could serve here is borrowing without waiting, so it is judged through borrow-wait if it is a means at all; it may instead be a veto. Asked in questions.

rejected.label: Supports many languages
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because the brochures list language counts. Asked in questions in case members need it.

anchors.text: A source states that a borrower must wait several days for a tool to be handed over.
A source states that a borrower can collect a tool within a day when it is available.
A source states that a borrower takes an available tool at once, by self-service check-out.

definition.objective: Members get a tool when they need it
definition.question: How long must a member wait to take a tool that is available?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of how a tool is borrowed and handed over; a review's remark about speed alone does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a tool is borrowed or handed over.
Sources disagree on how long a handover takes.

exclusions: Has a mobile app: judge the wait to borrow, not the device.
The number of tools in the library; that is not about waiting.

anchors.text: A source states that the platform does not record who has borrowed a tool.
A source states that the platform records each loan, but shows who holds a tool only through a loan history that must be searched.
A source states that the platform shows, for each tool, who holds it now and since when.

definition.objective: The society's tools are not lost
definition.question: Can the society see, for one tool, who has it now?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of its loan records and what those records show; a claim that loans are tracked without saying who holds a tool does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes what the platform records about loans.
Sources disagree on whether the platform records who holds a tool.

exclusions: Who can see the holder: asked in questions, not judged here.
Whether a tool is returned on time; that is a behaviour of members, not of the platform.

provenance.quote: Members should be able to borrow a tool without waiting days.
We want to know who has which tool so nothing goes missing.

questions: You said the platform needs a mobile app. No reason was given. Is that a hard requirement, so that a platform without one is ruled out whatever else it does, or a way of borrowing quickly that is judged above?
Who should be able to see who has which tool: the administrators only, or all members? Members' names are personal information.
Do members need the app in languages other than English? The brochures list between 9 and 20.
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
Only two criteria come from what you said. Is there anything else the society wants the platform to do?

objectives.text: The group knows the route before the walk

rejected.label: Exports GPX files
rejected.note: The user gave no reason for the requirement. The only objective it could serve here is sharing the route in advance, so it is judged there if it is a means at all; it may instead be a veto. Asked in questions.

rejected.label: Social feed
rejected.note: The user said: 'Nobody cares about the social feed.'

rejected.label: Badges and achievements
rejected.note: Nobody raised it, and all three brochures list badges, so it would not separate them.

rejected.label: Offline maps
rejected.note: Nobody raised it; only one brochure lists it. Asked in questions in case walkers need maps without a signal.

rejected.label: Elevation profiles
rejected.note: Nobody raised it; only one brochure lists it.

rejected.label: Weather overlay
rejected.note: Nobody raised it; only one brochure lists it.

criteria.label: Share a route before the walk

anchors.text: A source states that a route can be shared only with other users of the app who follow the leader.
A source states that a route can be shared by a link, but the link opens only in the app.
A source states that a route can be sent to anyone, app user or not, by a link or a file.

definition.objective: The group knows the route before the walk
definition.question: Can a leader send the route to group members before the walk, and to whom?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation or product page describing how a route is shared; a reviewer's general praise of the app does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a route is shared.
Sources disagree about who a route can be shared with.

exclusions: Exports GPX files: judge the sharing, not the file format; the GPX requirement is asked in questions.
Social feed: the user said nobody cares about it.

provenance.quote: Leaders need to share a route with the group the evening before.

questions: The user said the app has to export GPX files. No reason was given. Is that a hard requirement, so that an app without GPX export is ruled out whatever else it does, or a way of sharing that is judged above?
Do walkers need the route or maps on the walk without a phone signal? One brochure offers offline maps and nobody has said whether it matters.
Only one criterion comes from what you said. Is there anything else the walk leaders need the app to do?
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled?
